steps: We picked 1 class: MATH 140.
We found the 1 safe place for an AI helper.
We also found where AI must stay out.
It is a geometry class at SCAD.
Students draw shapes and write proofs.
The class lasts 10 weeks.
A proof is a list of steps.
Each step has a reason.
A reason is a math rule. It is not a picture.
Can geometry students fixing their own proofs…
…use an AI that points only at the first weak step…
…to find mistakes before the quiz…
…while every step stays theirs and only the teacher grades?
🌱 1 Draw: draw by hand.
🌿 2 Write: write your own proof.
💧 3 Hint: get 1 hint. The only AI stop.
🌸 4 Explain: explain out loud.
🍓 5 Quiz: show what you know.
Each stop is a garden stage: seed, sprout, water, bloom, fruit.
The AI hint is the water.
A little water helps a plant grow.
Too much water drowns it. A hint that gives the answer is too much.
Only at Stop 3, the hint helper.
There is no AI when you draw, explain, or take the quiz.

questions.q: What does the hint helper do?
steps: You paste a proof that you wrote.
It points at the first weak step.
It names the kind of rule to look up.
It asks you 1 question.

questions.q: What can the hint helper NOT do?
steps: It cannot write a step.
It cannot give the answer.
It cannot say that a proof is correct.
It cannot give grades.
It cannot see drawings.

questions.q: Why must I write 2 steps first?
steps: The ideas must be yours.
The helper only checks work that exists.
So it cannot start the proof for you.

questions.q: What if a hint is wrong?
steps: Pick Not sure or I disagree.
The hint goes to the teacher's list.
The teacher checks it in 2 days. This is before you present.
If it was wrong, the teacher tells you.

questions.q: Who is responsible for a wrong hint?
steps: The teacher.
The teacher picks the tool.
The teacher checks every unsure hint.
The practice helper saves nothing.
Start over clears everything.
The live helper sends only your proof text.
Do not paste your name or ID.

Our team wrote the hint first.
No real AI made it.

🌱 Draw: the teacher.
🌿 Write: the student.
💧 Hint: the teacher, for unsure hints.
🌸 Explain: the teacher.
🍓 Quiz: the teacher gives all grades.
The partner is a classmate. 🐝
They ask "why?" when you explain at the board.
They do not grade.

questions.q: What if I have no computer?
steps: Use the paper rule list. 📗
Go to the teacher's office hours.
It counts the same as the AI way.
Help is slower. That is a real gap.
Kids with no computer at home.
Kids who use a screen reader. The helper cannot see drawings.
The paper rule list keeps it fair.
1. Students: they use it.
2. The teacher: the boss.
3. Partners and tutors: people nearby.
4. People who can be left out.
5. People who get hurt if it goes wrong.

questions.q: What did the Bastani study find?
steps: About 1,000 high school students used AI for math.
Open ChatGPT: 17% worse on the real test later.
Hints-only AI: no drop.
So our helper gives hints only.

questions.q: What did the Kestin study find?
steps: College physics students used a teacher-built AI tutor.
They learned more than in a normal class.
Physics is not geometry. We must still test it.

questions.q: What did the Petrov study find?
steps: Experts graded AI proofs on hard contest problems.
Most AIs got less than 5% right.
But the AIs sounded sure.
So the AI never grades.

questions.q: What did the build tests find?
steps: 16 checks ran. 16 passed.
1 hole: Start over brings back a stopped helper.
An AI ran the checks. People must test it too.

questions.q: What is the Start over hole?
steps: You can stop the helper if a hint gives away a step.
But Start over clears everything, the stop too.
So the helper comes back. We must fix this.

questions.q: Is the quiz open book or no computers?
steps: The syllabus says each exam is open book.
Our map says Stop 5 has no computers.
Ask the teacher which rule is true.
Part 1 🌱: draw a line that cuts a segment in half.
Part 2 🌿: write a proof with reasons.
Part 3 💧: the AI points at 1 weak step.
Part 4 🌸: flip a triangle to explain.
Part 5 🍓: build the golden ratio.
